The manual initialize/copy/check gate shares the local operation lock, verifies target owner/mode, proves exact source snapshot coverage through restic's preserved original lineage, writes a private receipt, and cannot delete remote data. The rotation gate uses an echo-disabled local terminal and inherited anonymous file descriptors; live acceptance preserved all three snapshots in both repositories, accepted the replacement password, rejected the previous password, and required no rollback. The replica path uses fixed key-only SSH/SFTP configuration, one optional init, restic copy, metadata check, and post-copy inventory. Restore terminates blocked_for_human_review and cannot promote staged data into live state.

items.title: Device-scoped fleet status, maintenance, and reboot control
items.summary: Track the workstation, Forge, the Pi-hole appliance, qualified Crucible, and optional read-only appliances through persistent status cards while restricting maintenance and reboot authority to explicitly supported devices.
items.implementation: The Guided Maintenance dashboard loads a private atomic fleet snapshot, separates SSH-integrated systems from compact status-only network presence, and exposes Maintenance and Reboot only on supported mutable cards. The owner machine uses the portable canonical ID workstation and an operator-configured display label; the former maven ID and environment names remain bounded read aliases only. The Operations Topology view reads one bounded local /proc/net/route projection and renders the primary network path as WAN/provider cloud → detected default gateway → detected local subnet → known devices; management, containment, DNS, provider, inventory, and planned backup relationships remain supplemental below it. A reviewed enrolled gateway supplies its identity and status, while an unmatched route produces an inert evidence-only node. Forge and Pi-hole operations use fixed SSH aliases and vectors. Crucible D1 adds a SHA-256-bound root helper exposing only self-check, one DNF5 upgrade, and one reboot; a failed self-check falls closed to inventory-only. All supported operations use fresh digest-bound previews, exact device confirmations, one global identity-checked lock, redacted receipts, and no automatic mutation retry. Reboot sends one request, requires a changed boot identity and fixed device-specific readiness, then replaces the snapshot. An optional Cisco 8851/Webex Calling card performs one bounded reachability probe, asserts no registration or firmware state, and has no mutation controls. Package evidence is capability-aware: Atelier synchronizes and queries a disposable alternate pacman database for official updates, uses `yay -Qua` for AUR-only updates, and removes the temporary metadata before returning; DNF5 and Flatpak remain on-demand, while privileged APT metadata remains explicitly cached. Deployment addresses live only in ignored environment configuration. A status-only systemd timer collects at noon and midnight.
items.technologies: Ruby bounded services and typed application operations; fakeroot and pacman alternate database; yay AUR-only query; OpenSSH fixed aliases; bounded ICMP appliance probes; APT, DNF5, Flatpak, and Pi-hole fixed vectors; Proxmox VE and LXC; JSON snapshots and receipts; SHA-256 digest binding; systemd user oneshot/timer; vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS Dashboard.
items.interfaces: Administration → Guided Maintenance; Collect fleet status; per-device Refresh with fresh or cached package-evidence labels; status-only appliance cards; supported per-device Maintenance and Reboot dialogs; evidence-driven Operations Topology network map; persisted status cards.

items.title: Portable Linux fleet discovery and capability enrollment
items.summary: Generalize Guided Maintenance from the Operator's reviewed fixed devices into an explicit subnet-discovery, review, and enrollment flow for supported Linux and appliance targets.
items.implementation: A1 accepts one human-selected private IPv4 subnet, performs one 30-second-bounded nmap discovery pass after an explicit click, and retains candidates only in the page session. Configured, enrolled, and ignored identities are excluded from actionable candidates. One bounded local ARP-table read and Nmap's OUI data add ephemeral MAC, vendor, interface, and neighbor-state hints. Only the last successful canonical subnet is remembered. Digest-reviewed enrollment writes one owner-private 0600 record; ignored candidates have a separate reversible private list. A4 removes only the enrolled or ignored address from the current scan results so remaining candidates can be reviewed sequentially without rescanning; restore and registry removal preserve unrelated candidates. Status-only enrollment may be fixed or DHCP-tracked by one reviewed MAC/subnet; SSH inventory remains fixed and requires one literal alias whose HostName equals the selected address. A guided prerequisite can request a validated remote account and existing owner-private key path, derive HostName from the reviewed candidate, preview one fixed non-interactive Host stanza, and atomically append it after a separate digest-bound click; it never stores credentials, establishes trust, enrolls the device, or grants mutation authority. A5 recognizes an enrolled PVE kernel plus fixed pveversion executable and collects bounded PVE version, cached APT updates, kernel/reboot, and guest evidence while retaining the exact enrolled identity and inventory-only control. A2 adds one bounded per-device Refresh and Checked timestamp. A3 verifies a tracked current-IP MAC, performs one bounded recovery scan on mismatch or absence, retargets only one exact status-only MAC match with bounded address history, and permits one transient ten-minute retry before backing off. Compact status-only cards show IP, assigned name, Online/Offline status, Refresh, checked time, probe, and reachability. Fleet states use green for Healthy/Online, yellow for Updates available, and red for Offline/Reboot required.
items.technologies: Ruby bounded command runner and typed discovery/status services; nmap host discovery and OUI database; Linux /proc IPv4 ARP evidence; fixed BatchMode OpenSSH inventory; IPAddr subnet validation; SHA-256 preview binding; atomic owner-private JSON; one hardened transient systemd-run user oneshot; capability vocabulary for pacman, yay, paru, apt/apt-get, dnf/dnf5, zypper, apk, Flatpak, Snap, and Nix; Dashboard JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and existing application envelope.
items.interfaces: Administration → Guided Maintenance → Discover & enroll a device; explicit subnet scan; candidate Review or Ignore; status-only fixed/DHCP or fixed SSH inventory enrollment; reversible ignored list; private registry removal; compact status-only and rich managed cards; per-device Refresh and Checked evidence; Makefile checks and deterministic verifiers.

A4 deterministic coverage proves exact-address removal and the absence of whole-list clearing after candidate or registry actions; on 2026-07-28 the Operator live-accepted sequential candidate action with the unrelated list preserved and no rescan. items.title: NixOS Temper maintenance laboratory

items.implementation: Temper is a NixOS 26.05 QEMU VM on Foundry with a pinned nixos-26.05 flake, key-only SSH, QEMU guest agent, disabled automatic upgrades/garbage collection, and one declarative root-owned helper. The fleet adapter recognizes immutable NixOS command paths, presents only the native Nix channel, compares the pinned nixpkgs revision with the live stable branch, and treats an active/booted generation mismatch as reboot evidence. Exact authority self-check evidence unlocks the shared device-scoped Maintain and Reboot controls. Upgrade performs one flake-lock update plus nixos-rebuild switch and restores the prior lock on failure; reboot remains separate. Invalid helper operations and broad sudo are rejected.
